version.changelog:
- Added a disclaimer section to clarify data accuracy and provide usage guidance.
- No changes to core features or functionality.

llm.summary: This is a straightforward currency-conversion skill that discloses its exchange-rate provider and does not show persistence, credential access, or hidden side effects.

dimensions.detail: Outbound HTTPS requests to open.er-api.com and local execution of the bundled Python script are proportionate to live exchange-rate lookup and are disclosed in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains only SKILL.md and one Python script, with no install hook, dependency installation, or package-manager behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger phrases are fairly broad and may activate for general exchange-rate questions, but that is still aligned with the skill's stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No file writes, credential access, privilege escalation, scheduled tasks, background workers, or persistent configuration changes were found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The documented purpose is currency conversion, rate lookup, comparison, and historical exchange-rate lookup; the bundled script only parses CLI arguments and queries the disclosed open.er-api.com API for those functions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, understand that currency codes, dates, and requested amounts may be used to query open.er-api.com, and the returned rates are informational rather than financial advice. The unused subprocess import should ideally be removed, but it is not used by the artifact.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The skill does use a shell-invoked local Python script and network access, but both are visible in SKILL.md and fit the exchange-rate lookup purpose; no broader runtime behavior was found.
[SQP-1] expected: The activation terms are broad, but they are all currency or exchange-rate related; this is a usability/scoping note rather than evidence of unsafe behavior.
[SQP-3] expected: The bilingual description matches the Chinese and English usage examples and does not create a security concern.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The subprocess import is unnecessary for the stated purpose, but inspection found it is unused and no subprocess calls are made.
[SQP-2] expected: The latest-rate request sends the user-selected currency code to open.er-api.com; the provider is disclosed in SKILL.md and the data shared is limited to rate-query parameters.
[SQP-2] expected: The historical-rate request sends the selected currency and date to the same disclosed provider; no unrelated data collection or exfiltration path was found.
